# P0.15j — fact-check citation-fetch discipline (eval + skill hardening; Stage A)

Implements `docs/tickets/16_P0.15j__fact-check-citation-discipline.md` (REQ-VIS-9 / §12.8(c) / §18).
Stacked on MAINT.1 (PR #26). Closes the **construction half** of `D-P0.15i-2`.

## Summary

A complete `second_read=false` Review runs all six required phases with real proxy-logged web research (P0.15i)
but delivery still throws `cited_not_fetched`: the fact-check cites authoritative URLs it produced from **training
knowledge** (snopes/scientificamerican/forbes/deadline) that never appear in the run's fetch log. The guard
`validateCitedFetched` is all-or-nothing — one un-retrieved citation fails the whole review — so it cannot tell
you *how close* a run is, and can't drive iteration.

This ticket builds the **measurement** and takes **Path A** (skill discipline; preferred). Path B (a harness
citation-backfill that relaxes cited⇒fetched semantics) is **not** taken — it needs an explicit operator ruling.

## What changed

- **Citation-fetch-compliance eval** (`packages/benchmark/src/scorers/citation-fetch.ts`, exported) — a
  deterministic §18 scorer: `citationFetchCompliance(claims, fetchedNormalizedUrls, normalize?)` reports the
  **fraction** of a claim ledger's cited URLs (`claim.url` + every `claim.sources[].url`) present in the run's
  proxy fetch log, the exact per-`(claim, url, which)` misses, and a `compliant` flag; `claimLedgerCompliance`
  scores a whole `01-claim-ledger.json`; `assertCitationComplianceFloor` is the regression guard. Its
  `normalizeCitedUrl` is byte-parity with the guard's `@rhema/mirror normalizeUrl` (pinned by a test), so the
  score measures exactly what delivery enforces; a live caller injects `normalizeUrl` for exact parity.
- **Fixtures + tests** (`citation-fetch.test.ts`, 8) — a disciplined dev fixture scores 100% (AC1 green); a
  fixture modelling the observed P0.15i failure flags every miss; dedup-denominator, empty-ledger, floor, and
  normalization-parity cases covered. `@rhema/mirror` added as a **test-only devDependency**.
- **Skill discipline (Path A(a))** — editorial-review verification-protocol gains **§6 "fetch-then-cite loop"**
  (before any ledger row, the source URL must be a search result or you `web_fetch` it now; otherwise the verdict
  is `Unverifiable` and the row carries no URL — a remembered famous-outlet URL or a link found *inside* a
  fetched page both count as un-retrieved), and Rule 5 points at it. Reconciled through the vendored pin → port
  (`check-upstream-diff.mjs` OK, only sanctioned edits) → `PROTOCOLS_VERSION` re-frozen `0.4.0+5856e59c…` →
  `0.4.0+5b08d37da59aad92`.

## Design decisions

- **Eval, not guard change.** `validateCitedFetched` is UNCHANGED (12/12 green, still fails an un-retrieved
  citation). The eval is a reporting layer over the same quantity — it hill-climbs the discipline without
  weakening the delivery bar.
- **Path A over Path B.** Path B relaxes the guard's meaning and requires an ADR/operator ruling; absent that
  ruling the preferred rigorous fix is skill discipline. The eval is now the instrument to decide, in Stage B,
  whether Path A(a) skill hardening + optionally **Path A(b)** (verification on `claude-opus-5`/`claude-fable-5`)
  converges to 100% — and only if it will not does Path B's ruling apply. Model routing is left unchanged offline
  (no offline proof possible; it's a Stage-B lever).
- **Parity without coupling.** The scorer keeps its own copy of the guard's normalization (so the §18 scoring
  layer takes no production dependency on the run-delivery layer) and a test-only devDep import pins byte-parity.
